headline: High-risk shared-workspace and server-side flow execution make Langflow→marker pair prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write/read the server filesystem and chain tools in flows, so attacker-controlled document content could be fed into downstream steps. Marker is a document processor with no isolation details, so if Langflow passes its outputs into marker, prompt-like content may be treated as instructions. The shared path is plausible but not proven by docs.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are passed into marker as text or files
IF marker processes untrusted document content without a provenance filter
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Langflow output before marker ingests it
Strip instruction-like prefixes from documents before handoff
Use a manual review step for any document that contains embedded prompts
requires-engineering: isolate the handoff through a sanitized queue
requires-engineering: add content-type validation between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and can egress broadly to APIs; marker has no declared filesystem or network access, but if it receives Langflow-produced files, sensitive content can be exposed in the workflow. The pair’s shared workspace/server-side state makes leakage plausible even though marker itself appears constrained.
conditions: IF Langflow stores uploaded files or intermediate outputs containing sensitive data
IF marker is given those files or text through the same workspace or API
mitigations: Remove secrets and PII from Langflow inputs before processing
Disable broad egress on Langflow flows that handle sensitive documents
Store sensitive artifacts in a separate workspace from marker
requires-engineering: enforce per-flow data classification controls
requires-engineering: add redaction before any cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has server-side filesystem write and subprocess execution, while marker has no write, shell, or network capabilities listed. That means direct write-write conflict is not evident; the main risk is only if deployment grants marker extra mutable access not shown here. Based on the profiles, overlap is limited and blast radius is small.
conditions: IF marker is deployed with additional write permissions not present in its profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep marker read-only
Separate the agents into different directories
Avoid concurrent writes from Langflow flows
requires-engineering: add file locking if shared storage is unavoidable

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, so its outputs may become marker inputs without a verification gate. Marker is a document-processing system, not a validator, so it may render or transform Langflow-produced content as if it were authoritative. This creates a default-path cascade, though not clearly an action-taking one.
conditions: IF marker consumes Langflow output without independent verification
IF Langflow-generated facts are used as source text for downstream document generation
mitigations: Insert a verification step before marker consumes Langflow output
Require citations or source links in Langflow outputs
Flag low-confidence Langflow outputs for manual review
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow explicitly handles per-flow component credentials and uploaded files, while marker’s profile shows no declared data classes or residency controls. The mismatch is mainly a documentation gap rather than a proven breach, so compliance risk is limited but real if regulated data is routed through Langflow into marker.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Langflow flows
IF marker processes the same regulated data without a documented retention or residency policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Document retention for Langflow uploads
Confirm marker’s storage and deletion behavior before use
requires-engineering: add a data-processing agreement review
requires-engineering: segregate regulated workloads from this pair
